evidence: Documentation-only changes; no scientific code, model, or release artifact changed on this branch.
Official CPVS Table2 ReadMe identifies Seq bytes 24-29 as the internal source identifier used by ztf2g/ztf2r; Table2 has 781602 rows but Seq values span 1..781604.
Heavy run 38095650470 read 730184 published names but mapped them to row ordinals; the reported 725101 intersection / 16686 candidate-only / 5083 published-only counts are invalid and superseded.

PR #176 now maps published names to actual Table2 Seq IDs in the independent audit and derives the parent ID universe from actual Seq; fresh heavy evidence has not completed at this documentation revision.
PR #176 also adds an explicit finite-SNR check because NaN < sigma is false, plus flag-zero diagnostics strictly as hypotheses. It does not alter published thresholds or production selection.
Documentation CI, product-scope audit, CodeQL, and lifecycle validation must pass on this branch's current head before merge.

root_causes: Troubleshooting and README had stale CPVS claims that treated invalid or pre-fix membership values as current evidence.
Product roadmap needed a canonical acceptance-driven entry point.

Historical membership audit first compared a Table4 catalog-internal ID directly to parent SourceID; later it joined names to physical Table2 row ordinals rather than the true Seq/SourceID. Both comparisons were semantically invalid.
The derivation also filtered candidate lightcurve SourceIDs against a row-ordinal parent ID universe, so its historical 741787 candidate count is not a verified current count.
A separate SNR guard bug allowed NaN values through because the prior comparison checked only snr < sigma; PR #176 now explicitly rejects non-finite SNR.

findings: A merged scientific correction is not full benchmark resolution until independent audit passes.
Workflow-level success with a skipped required job does not establish scientific release readiness.
Product completion requires end-to-end user acceptance, not feature presence alone.
Catalog identifier semantics must come from the publisher schema; physical row order is not a valid replacement for a Seq/SourceID key.
A parser can read every published name correctly yet still produce an invalid comparison if it maps names into the wrong identifier space.
A zero-row parse of an external reference is an input-format failure; never interpret it as a real empty reference set.
NaN comparisons are false: scientific threshold guards must explicitly reject non-finite SNR values, not rely only on a less-than comparison.
Flag-zero variants are diagnostic hypotheses only unless the published selection documentation establishes that flag policy.
